chunks: Sa'd ibn Abdillah from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab from Yazid ibn Ishaq Sha'ir from Harun ibn Hamzah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I heard him (peace be upon him) say: 'When you fast upon sighting the crescent and break your fast upon sighting it, you have completed the fasting of the month, even if you did not fast except for twenty-nine days. For the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: "The month is like this, like this, and like this," and he indicated with his hand to ten and ten and nine.'

key_terms.أَكْمَلْتَ صِيَامَ شَهْرٍ: you completed the fasting of the month

ai.seo_question: How many days are required to complete the fast of Ramadan if the month is twenty-nine days?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that completing the fast for twenty-nine days upon sighting the crescent is valid, reflecting the Prophet’s (PBUH) gesture indicating a month can be twenty-nine or thirty days. This hadith underscores the flexibility in lunar calendar calculations within Shia jurisprudence, emphasizing that the obligation is fulfilled even if the month is not thirty days, provided the sighting occurs. It highlights the practical application of *ru'yah* (sighting) as the primary determinant for the start and end of Ramadan.
